findings.title: --manifest is required for gate/dev-tally/b3-aggregate/harness-verdicts, so the documented commands exit 2 and the active-manifest fallback never runs
findings.problem: _common(p, manifest_required=True) is the default, and only `list` passes False. The README documents `freeze_tally.py gate --gate <gate> --runs-root <R>` without --manifest; argparse rejects that and main() returns 2. _context() has `args.manifest or _active_manifest_path(series_dir)`, which is meant to pick the highest-N manifest, but it cannot be reached for these subcommands. It fails closed, but the documented release-gate invocation does not work.
findings.fix_hint: make --manifest optional for every subcommand (_context already resolves the active manifest), or fix the README commands
findings.why_it_matters: The gate command as documented always exits with a usage error.

findings.title: Auto-memory move uses an unvalidated, hardcoded PARKDIR; an empty value moves the memory dir to /<repo>-written-...
findings.problem: PD comes from sed over a hardcoded ~/.b3/phase54-live-memory-park.env, with no check that the file exists or that PD is non-empty and a directory. If restore-memory already ran, or the env file is missing, PD is empty and the mv target becomes '/<CP>-written-during-live-...': the move fails on macOS or misplaces the evidence. mem_evidence in common.sh does validate PD. Hardcoding the phase54 filename instead of $MEMPARK_ENV also breaks the Phase-55 runbooks that inherit this driver.
findings.fix_hint: guard `test -n "$PD" && test -d "$PD"` (die otherwise) and read the park env path from the runbook rather than hardcoding phase54
findings.why_it_matters: Evidence of memory written during a measured session can be lost or misplaced.
source_window: echo "RUN_CASE: clone auto-memory dir created by the session ($(find "$M" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ') files) moved to evidence"

members.title: Frozen run_case.sh hard-codes Phase-54 memory-park and transcript paths, so later windows break unless a new manifest is issued
members.problem: run_case.sh takes RUNBOOK from the environment, and its README says later-window runbooks will be built from RUN-PHASE54-live.md. But the post-run memory move reads the hard-coded `$HOME/.b3/phase54-live-memory-park.env`, not the runbook's MEMPARK_ENV. The NVW grep reads the hard-coded `runs-phase54-live/` (line 106). In a Phase-55 window that env file may not exist, PD is then empty and `mv "$M" "/$CP-written-..."` targets the filesystem root. That fails under `set +e`, so the clone's auto-memory is left in place, which is the known measurement confound. The next pre block's mem_evidence partly mitigates this. The directory is in freeze_manifest.COVERED, so fixing it after freeze is an identity change that needs a new manifest.
source_window: echo "RUN_CASE: clone auto-memory dir created by the session ($(find "$M" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ') files) moved to evidence"
members.why_it_matters: Phase 55 measurement depends on this runner. A late fix forces a manifest reissue, and an unfixed one risks auto-memory contaminating measured runs.
members.fix_hint: use $MEMPARK_ENV and $ARCHIVE from the runbook's common block, and refuse when PD is empty, before the Phase-55 manifest is issued

findings.title: Holdout measurement session launches with full-env inheritance, auto-approve permissions and no OS sandbox
findings.problem: `LAUNCH_ARGV` launches the measured `claude` session with `--permission-mode dontAsk` (line 90), so Bash/Write/Edit tool calls execute without any permission prompt. `session_environment()` (docs/design/holdout-v2.12/tools/holdout_eval_launch.py ~line 185-191) builds the session's environment as `os.environ` minus only `STRIPPED_ENV` — a 6-item Anthropic-auth-specific denylist defined in holdout_autopilot.py:110-112 (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`, `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`). Any other secret the owner's Terminal environment carries (GitHub tokens, cloud credentials, SSH agent vars, unrelated API keys) is passed through unfiltered. The settings file used for this launch (`docs/design/b3-ground-truth/b3-runner-v2.12/settings-measured.json`) carries no `sandbox`/network-blocking key at all (contrast with the fix-harness's explicit `network: {allowedDomains: [], strictAllowlist: true}` Seatbelt policy). The session reviews holdout case content that is, by the kit's own design, security/vulnerability-themed material.
findings.fix_hint: switch session_environment() to an explicit allowlist of the env keys the session actually needs (mirroring freeze_manifest.ENV_ALLOWLIST) rather than a denylist of Anthropic-auth keys only, and add an explicit sandbox/network-block policy (as harness_sandbox.build_session_settings does) to the runner settings template used for this launch.
findings.why_it_matters: If the reviewed content manages to prompt-inject the model into running a Bash command (no permission gate blocks this under `dontAsk`), any non-Anthropic secret present in the owner's environment can be read and, absent a network sandbox, exfiltrated — a class of attack indirect prompt injection against LLM review agents is known to enable.

findings.title: B3 measured review session pre-authorizes Bash/Write/Edit via --allowedTools with inherited shell environment and no OS sandbox
findings.problem: The `session` block execs `claude --permission-mode manual ... --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Grep,Glob,Task,Agent"`. `--allowedTools` pre-authorizes those tools, so despite `--permission-mode manual`, Bash/Write/Edit calls do not raise a permission card for `run_case.sh`'s die()-on-unexpected-card logic to catch. The `launch` block starts this process with `env "REPO=$REPO" ... bash -c "$SESSION_SHELL" ...` (common.sh, `launch` block) — `env` without `-i` adds those vars on top of, rather than replacing, whatever environment the tmux-server-launching shell already had, which the runbook itself documents at length ("a tmux pane inherits the environment of whichever shell started the tmux server"). Unlike the fix-harness (harness_sandbox.build_session_settings, which sets `network: {allowedDomains: [], strictAllowlist: true}` and a custom per-call `can_use_tool` gate), no OS-level sandbox or outbound-network restriction is configured anywhere in settings-measured.json or this runbook for the B3 session.
findings.fix_hint: give the B3 measured session the same kind of OS-level sandbox/network-block policy the fix-harness uses, and/or scope its environment to an explicit allowlist instead of inheriting the launching shell's environment plus overrides.
findings.why_it_matters: A B3 case that successfully prompt-injects the reviewing model gets unprompted Bash execution in an environment that includes whatever the owner's shell/tmux server environment holds, with no sandbox blocking outbound network — a realistic path to secret exfiltration from the operator's own machine.
source_window: test ! -e "$MEM" || { echo "AUTO-MEMORY FOR $CLONE IS NOT PARKED — STOPPING"; exit 1; }

findings.title: Holdout launcher calls the freeze kit's private git helpers _ls_tree and _cat_blobs
findings.problem: `materialize_plugin_from_candidate` lives in the holdout kit but calls `freeze_common._ls_tree` and `freeze_common._cat_blobs`, both underscore-private helpers of a different kit. The freeze kit's public helpers are `tree_files_at` and `blob_at`, and neither returns blob bytes for a whole tree. So the launcher depends on the freeze kit's internal batch format: the `(mode, kind, oid, path)` tuple order and the `--batch` parser.
findings.current_code:
entries = fcm._ls_tree(repo, sha, PLUGIN_REL)
...
    blobs = fcm._cat_blobs(repo, [oid for _m, _k, oid, _p in entries])
findings.fix_hint: add a public freeze_common helper (e.g. tree_blobs_at(repo, rev, prefix) -> {rel: (mode, bytes)}) and have the launcher call that
findings.why_it_matters: Any refactor of freeze_common's private tuple order or parser breaks the holdout measurement launcher. A change to freeze-kit tools also counts as engineering+detection+workflow under PATH-MAP, so the breakage would only show up as a new candidate and a full rerun.

raise KitError("%s is empty or absent at %s" % (PLUGIN_REL, sha))

findings.title: freeze_tally drives score43 through its private _require_complete and _cmd_dev_tally
findings.problem: freeze_tally is the one gate in front of every release tally, and it lives in docs/design. It calls `score43._require_complete(ledger)` and `score43._cmd_dev_tally(view, require_fingerprint=want)`, which are underscore-private internals of a plugin script. `b3-aggregate` goes through the public `score43.run([...])`, but the completeness gate and dev-tally bypass it. pending: confirm score43 has no public equivalent of these two functions (score43.py was not readable from this lane).
findings.fix_hint: expose public score43 entry points (e.g. require_complete, dev_tally) or route through score43.run([...]) with an argv
findings.why_it_matters: A private rename in score43 silently breaks the release-gate tally path. The freeze README names this as the only path that may count runs.

findings.title: Third implementation of building the plugin copy from the candidate commit, with diverging rules

intent_doc_match.quote: Every runner materializes its plugin copy from the candidate commit via git (`git archive` or a worktree at the candidate), never from the working tree.

findings.problem: The diff writes the same operation three times. (1) common.sh `b3_materialize_runner` uses `git archive | tar -x`. (2) harness_sandbox.py `snapshot_plugin_from_commit` has its own `_tree_entries` and a second `_cat_blobs` parser (freeze_common already has one). (3) holdout_eval_launch.py `materialize_plugin_from_candidate` uses freeze_common's private helpers. The copies already behave differently: the harness and holdout copies refuse symlinks and keep only 100644/100755, while the B3 tar extraction accepts symlinks. The holdout docstring also claims 'no export attribute can alter it', a property the B3 git-archive path does not have (no .gitattributes is tracked today).
findings.fix_hint: one public freeze_common materializer (ls-tree + cat-file, regular files only) used by the harness and the holdout launcher, with B3 calling it via python3 instead of git archive
findings.why_it_matters: Three runners produce the measured copy under three slightly different rules. A future .gitattributes or symlink in plugins/vibe-check would change only the B3 copy, and the identity check would then refuse B3 alone.
